transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-05-12
Start time: 09:34 PT
Duration: 47 minutes (recorded)
Attendees: Avery Collins (Redwood AE), Diego Ramirez (Redwood SE), Harper Liu (CSM); Maya Chen, Rohit Patel, Sofia Alvarez, Evan Brooks (Nebula Retail)

Auto-generated summary (may be imperfect):
Nebula wants to bump committed capacity ~20% across their checkout inference and enable APAC + EU regions. They want an EU on-prem pilot for data-residency, plus KMS integration and audit logs. Pricing options discussed: seat-based vs usage; procurement asks for redlined SOW and standard PO timeline.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Avery: Good morning everyone, thanks for joining, uh I'll kick us off. Maya, thanks for taking time. Quick agenda: contract amendment, capacity sizing, EU on-prem pilot and APAC activation timeline.
[00:22] Maya: Yeah thanks Avery. We had a leadership sync last week, they're asking to move forward with an uplift but want the EU on-prem pilot gated before full activation for EU. Also procurement wanted clarity on pricing model.
[00:45] Rohit: Hey all, from eng side the checkout latency is the main SLO, so if we move to Dedicated we need to keep p50 under 60ms for typical browse+cart flows — is that still realistic?
[01:12] Diego: Short answer: yes, with the right pool sizing and batching config we can hit that. There are tradeoffs, um, between throughput cost. At high qps continuous batching helps cost but can add a few ms. We'll show numbers in the benchmark.
[01:37] Sofia: For security, can you confirm support for customer-managed KMS and HSM? Our auditors want to see key rotation and separation of duties.
[01:55] Avery: Right, so Redwood Private supports customer KMS in the Private plane, and for Dedicated we can integrate with cloud KMS or HSM — Diego, correct me if I'm messing the terms.
[02:12] Diego: Yeah, so for EU on-prem we can either ship the private control plane and integrate with your HSM on-prem, or if you run in a VPC we can do customer-managed KMS via our connectors. Small caveat: some of the rotation automation is handled by Redwood Console; if you need full manual rotation we can disable automation. There's some follow-up work to document exact key policies.
[02:45] Evan: Procurement note — timeline wise we need updated pricing and a redlined SOW to start internal approvals. Ideally by end of week.
[03:02] Avery: Okay we can do that. I'll share a redline and updated pricing spreadsheet by Thursday, 5/14.
[03:17] Maya: On the EU on-prem pilot, we want a two-week validation with our data and a small sample of traffic, so we can prove latency and correctness before scale. What's involved to get that provisioned?
[03:35] Diego: Provisioning EU on-prem pilot requires environment access, some infra pre-reqs (network, firewall rules, certs). If we do dedicated on your cloud account it takes ~5-7 business days once we have infra access; fully on-prem (air-gapped) shipping the appliance might add 2-3 weeks. For the test pool we can spin up a reserved pool equivalent to 2x A100 performance in hosted or dedicated within a few days.
[04:05] Rohit: So if we wanted APAC enabled as well what's the lead time? We have a datacenter in APAC we prefer to use.
[04:22] Diego: APAC depends on region. If it's cloud-hosted (public region) we can enable in ~3 business days. If you want private or on-prem in APAC that will be longer — depends on logistics. We do have partners to help with hardware.
[04:43] [crosstalk] Maya: Mm-hmm.
[04:48] Harper: Quick note — we ran a usage analysis and a 20% committed uplift looks aligned with their growth forecasts. We'll include a recommended buffer for peak days.
[05:05] Maya: That makes sense. On pricing, can you show seat-based vs usage with examples for monthly QPS 10k vs 30k?
[05:21] Avery: Yes, I'll include two scenarios in the spreadsheet: flat seat-based committed with discounts, and usage tiered with overage. Highlighted callouts for caching and batching assumptions.
[05:36] Sofia: Also security checklist — SOC2, ISO status? We have a legal checklist.
[05:45] Avery: Redwood is SOC 2 Type II — our public reports are in the security portal. For ISO we are in progress, Diego might have timeline.
[05:56] Diego: We're working on ISO 27001 certification, expected mid-2025. In the meantime we can provide architecture diagrams, audit logging details and how we retain request traces in the Console. Note: some artifact names may show Redwood internals that the auditors sometimes misread.
[06:18] Rohit: For the bench, can you run synthetic traces that include long context (1k tokens) for our recommendation? We use long product descriptions which blow up token counts.
[06:32] Diego: Absolutely. We'll include 1k token and 2k token profiles in the bench plan. Also we'll test kv cache hit patterns — sometimes the K V cache (transcribed as K V cash earlier in notes) behavior can change latency.
[06:50] Maya: Minor ask — can we try quantized model variants? We want cost savings but need no regression in checkout outputs.
[06:58] Diego: Yes, Redwood Optimize can recommend quantization profiles. We'll run quality evals tied to your prompt set to ensure parity. If there's drift we'll show rollback plan.
[07:12] Evan: Procurement: payment terms — we prefer net 60 on enterprise contracts. Is that something you can accept?
[07:22] Avery: Standard is net 30 but we can negotiate on the amendment; put that in the redline and we'll escalate.
[07:34] Maya: On SLA, our engineering leadership wants an uptime SLA and a clearly defined escalation path for latency regressions.
[07:43] Harper: For Dedicated we already offer SLA-backed uptime and latency targets per the contract. We'll include escalation contacts and runbook references in the SOW appendix.
[07:58] Sofia: Also auditors asked for proof of audit log immutability, retention windows — do you support exporting logs to our SIEM?
[08:08] Diego: Yes, we can stream audit logs to customer SIEM via secure forwarders; retention windows are configurable in Console. One thing: in on-prem setups logs may be stored locally and you'd be responsible for long-term retention depending on the deployment model.
[08:28] Rohit: For the capacity uplift — what's the recommended pool sizing if we want p50 under 60ms at peak 30k QPS?
[08:41] Diego: Ballpark: that workload with 1k token median might need something like 10-ish A100 equivalents if we assume 80% KV cache efficiency; that's a rough calc. We'll provide a precise right-sized plan after the benchmark run.
[09:02] Maya: Can you do a cost estimate for a mixed model: EU on-prem for compliance-critical flows, Hosted for US traffic, and Dedicated for APAC?
[09:17] Avery: We'll produce a blended estimate and show tradeoffs — cost, latency, operational overhead.
[09:27] Evan: Procurement follow-up: send commercial terms and proposed amendments so legal can start redlining.
[09:35] Avery: Noted. We'll push the redline by 5/14.
[09:40] [pause]
[09:48] Maya: One question on telemetry — will Redwood Console show per-route token-level costs across regions? We need that for cost allocation to product teams.
[09:58] Diego: Yes, Console offers token-level breakdowns and per-route/model dashboards. Slight caveat: in on-prem you may need extra agents to forward per-route metrics into our Console; we'll document that.
[10:23] Rohit: Any blockers from your side to start the EU pilot?
[10:29] Diego: Just infra access and certs, and Sofia's list of compliance artifacts. Once we have that we can schedule the bench.
[10:42] Sofia: I'll email the compliance artifact list by Friday.
[10:48] Maya: Good. Also do you support per-customer model pinning and automatic fallback to smaller variants when latency spikes?
[10:57] Diego: Yep we have routing policies — pin to a model version, can fallback to a quantized or smaller variant automatically. We'll include examples in the bench plan.
[11:14] Evan: Any mention from competitors? We briefly evaluated LargeCloudAI but their pricing surprised us; curious if Redwood can match regional pricing.
[11:25] Avery: We'll include competitor benchmarking in the commercial appendix.
[11:33] Maya: Ok let's recap and next steps.
[11:36] Avery: Recap: We're aiming for a 20% committed uplift, EU on-prem 2-week pilot, APAC activation planning, redlined SOW and updated pricing by 5/14, benchmark run plan by 5/16, and provisioning window for dedicated test pool week of 5/20.
[11:58] Rohit: That works. Can we tentatively book the kickoff for 5/21?
[12:05] Avery: Sure I'll propose a 60-minute slot for the kickoff; Diego and Harper will lead technical onboarding.
[12:15] Maya: Great, thanks everyone.
[12:19] [end recording]
